title: I2C Five-Device Sensor Fusion
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning MicroPython
description: Five I2C devices (MPU-6050 accelerometer and gyroscope, VL53L0X distance, INA219 battery monitor, SSD1306 display) share one bus. A to-scale timeline shows the display frame blocking sensor reads, and a complementary filter fuses accelerometer and gyroscope data.

educational.topic: I2C bus scheduling and sensor fusion
learningObjectives: Analyze how several I2C devices share one bus, using byte counts and bus speed to compute transaction time
Explain how a display update delays sensor reads and name two ways to fix it
Explain why accelerometer and gyroscope readings are fused into one estimate
prerequisites: I2C Bus Scanner and I2C Two Sensors in a Maze MicroSims

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Controlled experiments on a scale-accurate timeline
keyQuestions: Which device uses the most bus time, and why?
What happens to the gyroscope reads when the display refreshes 20 times a second at 100 kHz?
Why is the fused angle better than either sensor alone?
commonMisconceptions: Slow devices do not affect fast ones (one slow transaction blocks the whole bus)
Sensors can simply be averaged (fusion weights each sensor by what it is good at)
assessmentOpportunities: Student calculates transaction time from bytes and bus speed
Student predicts the effect of changing bus speed or display rate
